evidence.note: Framed work as pipeline stages (lexer/parser/codegen) not feature milestones, and wrote ALL modules at once including struct/union/preprocessor — attempting the whole language in one push (anchor-0 behavior) rather than a dependency-ordered feature progression.

After rewrite, retreated to a genuinely incremental loop: got 'return 42' working, tested 00001/00003/00006/00009, found locals broken → added Stmt::Decl, fixed division. Loose feature-layering (return-int → variables → arithmetic), the sensible-stages pattern of anchor 5.

Ran full suite, checked a subset (12/20 on first c-testsuite tests), examined failing tests to identify next features (pointers/arrays/structs). Progress checked against test subsets, but reactively by test number — no pre-defined per-milestone done-signals or dependency-ordered plan.
Hundreds of steps consumed by terminal-stuck recovery (Ctrl+C, kill processes, restore gcc); the feature-milestone thread is largely lost across the whole middle of the horizon.

Near the end still fixing features opportunistically (global struct .data emission, test 00047 hang) driven by individual failing tests rather than a maintained milestone ladder; no milestone hierarchy ever recorded.

reasoning: The agent began by attempting the whole language at once (anchor 0), but after collapse it adopted a sensible incremental loop — simplest programs first, then variables/arithmetic, then feature fixes guided by failing-test subsets — which reaches toward anchor 5. However it never maintained an explicit dependency-ordered milestone plan with named done-signals (anchor 8), the feature ordering was reactive to test numbers rather than deliberately dependency-sequenced, and the thread was largely lost across a huge mid-trajectory terminal-recovery derailment. This places it between anchors 3 and 5, at a 4.
